chunks: Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I hear the narration from you, so do I add and decrease (words)? He said: If you intend its meanings, then there is no harm.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to change the wording of a hadith while transmitting it?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of *al-riwayah bi al-ma'na* (transmission by meaning) rather than strict verbatim recitation, a foundational principle in Shia hadith sciences that prioritizes semantic fidelity over literal wording. It reflects the scholarly understanding that the essence of the Imam's teaching is preserved even if the linguistic structure varies, provided the core message remains unchanged. This flexibility facilitated the accurate transmission of religious knowledge across different generations and dialects.
